newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE BREAKS HEARTS WITH DOUBLE STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE BREAKS HEARTS WITH DOUBLE STRIKE.

text.p: England midfielder Paul Gascoigne stunned Hearts with two goals in 90 seconds to fire Glasgow Rangers to a 4-3 Scottish League Cup final triumph on Sunday.
Gascoigne's strikes in the 64th and 66th minutes came soon after their Edinburgh rivals had pulled back to 2-2 and seemed to have a great opportunity to end their 34 years without a trophy.
Steve Fulton and John Robertson hauled Hearts level at Celtic Park after Rangers seized a 2-0 lead with two goals from Scotland marksman Ally McCoist.
Yet although they scored a last-minute third goal through David Weir, there was no end to the Edinburgh team's wait for a first trophy since 1962.
Gascoigne, who is seeking to resolve personal problems, said: "This has helped make up for the last few weeks, but I've still got to make it up to my wife."
The England international, who has undergone counselling since admitting he assaulted his wife, Sheryl, added: "Hopefully this can be a turning point.
"Things have been going better for me off the pitch, and in the last few weeks, I've been more confident on the pitch as well."
Victory gave Rangers' manager Walter Smith his 11th outright trophy win and cleared a first hurdle towards a possible domestic treble.
The match was a personal triumph, too, for 34-year-old
McCoist, who took his scoring tally to eight in finals of this competition and extended his individual winners' medal record to nine.
McCoist struck first in the 11th minute, Dane Brian Laudrup setting up the goal with a weaving run from the right touchline.
McCoist headed his side 2-0 ahead from close range in the 27th minute, but Hearts earned a foothold in the final minute of the first half through Steve Fulton from a short corner.
Hearts equalised in the 59th minute of a thrilling final as John Robertson stabbed home a Neil McCann cross beyond goalkeeper Andy Goram.
But Gascoigne broke Hearts with his double strike shortly afterwards, bending a shot home from 20 metres and then working a neat one-two with Charlie Miller before slotting the ball home.
Weir gave Hearts hope with his 90th minute goal, headed in from a free kick on the right, but Rangers played out the minute of injury time to lift the Cup.
